title: How do we take away when there are no hundredths?
description: A length with no hundredths has one tenth broken into ten hundredths so that seven hundredths can be taken away. The answer is checked by changing both lengths to hundredths. Keeko takes seven away from nothing the wrong way round.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a place has too few, break one from the next bigger place. Watch for students who write seven hundredths because nothing from seven is seven.

source: Find 25 9/10 - 6 4/10 7/100, then check it by converting both numbers to hundredths.
video_script.why: The child can add tenths and hundredths with carrying and now takes one length from another by breaking a tenth.
video_script.substitution: When a place has too few to take away from, break one from the next bigger place.
video_script.anchor: A length of 25 9/10 with no hundredths, and 6 4/10 7/100 to be taken away from it, in columns of units, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_answer: nineteen and five tenths and seven hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes 0 from 7 in the hundredths place and writes 7, but there are no hundredths to take 7 from, so a tenth must be broken first.
video_script.payoff_line: The answer is nineteen units, four tenths, and three hundredths

final_answer.spoken: nineteen units, four tenths, and three hundredths

never_show: 7 hundredths written as the hundredths of the answer
maths_rules: 25 9/10 has no hundredths and 7 must be taken away, so break 1 tenth into 10 hundredths.
Check: 25 9/10 = 2590 hundredths, 6 4/10 7/100 = 647 hundredths, 2590 - 647 = 1943 hundredths = 19 43/100 = 19 units, 4 tenths, 3 hundredths.
Slip: 0 - 7 is not 7; a tenth must be broken to give 10 hundredths.
video_script.design: One idea: break a tenth into ten hundredths when there are too few hundredths. Assumes the child can write tenths and hundredths. Wrong idea: take the smaller digit from the bigger one in a place. The columns stay on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='top'/>We have a length of twenty five and nine tenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we take away six units, four tenths, and seven hundredths from it?

narration: <bookmark mark='break'/>When a place has too few to take away from, we break one from the next bigger place.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>One tenth breaks into ten hundredths.

marks.given: the two lengths are written in columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twenty five and nine tenths, and six units, four tenths, and seven hundredths to take away.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the difference, and then check it.

beats.on_screen: Hundredths: 0 hundredths in 25 9/10, but 7 to take away

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, look at the hundredths. The top number has no hundredths, but seven must be taken away.

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, break one tenth into ten hundredths. Nine tenths becomes eight tenths and ten hundredths.

marks.units: the tenths and the units are subtracted and 4 and 19 are written under their columns

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, subtract place by place. Ten take away seven leaves three hundredths.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Eight take away four leaves four tenths, and twenty five take away six leaves nineteen units.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2590 - 647 = 1943 hundredths; 1943 hundredths = 19 units and 43 hundredths; 43 hundredths = 4 tenths and 3 hundredths

marks.four: both numbers change to hundredths, 2590 and 647, and 2590 - 647 = 1943 is written
marks.back: 1943 hundredths changes back to 19 units and 43 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, check in hundredths. The first length is two thousand five hundred ninety hundredths, and the second is six hundred forty seven.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Their difference is one thousand nine hundred forty three hundredths, which is nineteen units and forty three hundredths.

marks.same: forty three hundredths splits into four tenths and three hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is nineteen units, four tenths, and three hundredths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Forty three hundredths is four tenths and three hundredths, so both ways match.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says nineteen and five tenths and seven hundredths, because nothing from seven is seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But we cannot take seven away from nothing. The top number has no hundredths, so one tenth must be broken first.
